exports.name: Affix
exports.description:
Pins its content to a viewport corner. `position` is a logical corner (default `bottom-end`), `offset` the distance
from the edges in px (default 20, plus the safe-area insets), `zIndex` its stacking (default 50). Portalled unless
`withinPortal={false}`. `render` replaces the element.

props.name: position
props.description: The corner, in logical terms (`end` is the right in left-to-right text).

props.name: offset
props.description: The distance from the edges in px, before the safe-area insets.

props.name: zIndex
props.description: The stacking order.

props.name: withinPortal
props.description: Render at the end of the body (or the portal container) instead of in place.

exports.name: BackToTop
exports.description:
A "back to top" button in a viewport corner, shown once `target` (default the window) has scrolled past `threshold`
px. Pressing it scrolls to the top, smoothly unless the user prefers reduced motion. `label` is the button's
accessible name and tooltip (default "Back to top"); `children` replaces the arrow icon. `scrolled` with
`onScrolledChange` controls whether it shows (for a host that tracks scrolling itself).

props.name: variant
props.description: The colour scheme and emphasis.

props.name: size
props.description: The height and padding; the `icon-*` sizes make a square button for a lone icon.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Busy: `aria-busy="true"` and `data-loading`, activation blocked but focus kept (focusable-disabled
semantics, so focus is not dropped mid-submit), full opacity. The children stay in place, invisible,
so the width does not jump, with a spinner centred over them. Controlled by this prop only.

props.name: render
props.description:
The primitives' render prop, an alias of `asChild` with the element given here instead of as the
child: an element (cloned with the button's props) or a function `(props) => element`. `asChild`
wins when both are given.

props.name: asChild
props.description:
Render the single child element instead of a `<button>`, merging the
button's props onto it (classes joined, handlers chained, the child's
other props win). Built on `useRender` from

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description:
Keep a disabled button in the tab order: `aria-disabled="true"` instead of `disabled`, clicks and
every key but Tab blocked (the primitive `useButton`), hover kept so a Tooltip can explain why.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description:
Whether the rendered element is a native `<button>`. Only read with `focusableWhenDisabled` or
`loading` (it decides `aria-disabled` vs `role="button"` handling). Defaults to true unless
`render`/`asChild` gives an element other than `<button>`.

props.name: loadingText
props.description: While `loading`, show the spinner beside this text instead of over the hidden children.

props.name: threshold
props.description: Show after scrolling this many px.

props.name: target
props.description: The scroll container to watch and scroll; default the window.

props.name: label
props.description: The button's accessible name and native tooltip.

props.name: scrolled
props.description: Whether the button shows (controlled); default it follows the scroll position.

props.name: onScrolledChange
props.description: Called when the scroll position crosses `threshold`, with whether it is past it.

props.name: children
props.description: The button's content.

props.name: affixClassName
props.description: Classes for the `Affix` around the button (`className` styles the button); `absolute` with `withinPortal={false}` pins it inside a positioned box.

props.name: offset
props.description: The distance from the edges in px, before the safe-area insets.

props.name: position
props.description: The corner, in logical terms (`end` is the right in left-to-right text).

props.name: withinPortal
props.description: Render at the end of the body (or the portal container) instead of in place.

props.name: zIndex
props.description: The stacking order.

exports.name: floatButtonVariants
exports.description:
The floating button's look on a `Button` (`size="icon"`): a shadow, the size and the shape. `xs` is Button's own 32px icon size
(BackToTop's, which follows a design language's button height); `sm` 40px, `default` 48px, `lg` 56px. `shape` `circle` is round,
`square` keeps the button slot's corner. `extended` (icon plus text) is as tall as the size and as wide as its text.
exports.signature: (props?: ({ size?: "default" | "xs" | "sm" | "lg" | null | undefined; shape?: "circle" | "square" | null | undefined; extended?: boolean | null | undefined; } & ClassProp) | undefined) => string

exports.name: AffixPosition
exports.description: A viewport corner, in logical terms.

exports.name: AlertDialogContent
exports.description:
The alert dialog. It opens with focus on its `AlertDialogCancel` when it has one (WAI-ARIA APG alertdialog: the least destructive action
takes focus, so an Enter pressed out of habit cancels instead of deleting); without one, the primitives' default (the first tab stop, or
the popup itself after a touch). `initialFocus` overrides it as on the primitive (`false`, `true`, a ref or a function).

props.name: initialFocus
props.description:
What to focus when the dialog opens: `false` nothing; `true` the first tab stop; an element (a ref); or a
function of how it was opened that returns an element, `true` for the default, or `false` for nothing.
Default: the popup itself when opened by touch (no on-screen keyboard), else the first tab stop.

props.name: finalFocus
props.description:
Where focus goes when the dialog closes: `false` nowhere; an element (a ref); or a function of how it
closed that returns an element, `true` for the default, or `false` for nothing. Default: the element that
had focus when it opened, else the trigger.

props.name: container
props.description: Where to render: an element, a shadow root, or a function that returns one. Default `document.body`.

props.name: size
props.description: The panel's width: `sm` is narrower and lays the footer's buttons out in two equal columns.

exports.name: AlertDialogDescription

exports.name: AlertDialogFooter

exports.name: AlertDialogHeader

exports.name: AlertDialogMedia

exports.name: AlertDialogOverlay

exports.name: maskApiKey
exports.description:
The masked form of a key: `showChars` characters kept on each side and dots between. A key too short to keep both ends is all dots.
With `maskLength` the dots are always that many (a short key becomes exactly `maskLength` dots), so the mask says nothing about the length.
exports.signature: (value: string, showChars: number, maskLength?: number) => string

exports.name: ButtonGroup
exports.description:
Joined buttons. Shares borders, rounds only outer corners (with the `button` slot's corner, so a design language rounds them as its buttons).

Children should be <Button> (or `ButtonGroupText` / `ButtonGroupSeparator`). The group layers `[&>*]`
selectors to collapse internal borders + neutralize per-button radii.

props.name: orientation
props.description:
The axis the buttons are joined along. `vertical` stacks them (full width each, outer corners top and
bottom). Written as `data-orientation`. The group keeps `role="group"`, which has no `aria-orientation`
in WAI-ARIA 1.2 (axe flags it), so the axis is not announced: a group of buttons is not a composite
widget with arrow keys, and each button is its own tab stop.

exports.name: ButtonGroupSeparator
exports.description:
A visible 1px seam between two joined buttons. Solid buttons have transparent borders, so two of them
butt into one block with no divider; this draws one.

Layout: the group pulls every child after the first back 1px, so the separator sits exactly on the pixel
the two buttons share and the group's width (or height) is the same with or without it. `z-15` keeps the
line above a hovered neighbour (z-10) but under a focused one (z-20), whose ring must not be cut.

Colour: after a solid button (`default`, `destructive`) the line is that button's foreground at 30%, a
light seam on the fill; after anything else (outline, secondary, ghost, text) it is the `border` token,
which on an outline group lies exactly on the shared border and changes nothing. The selector reads the
Button's own `data-variant`, so no prop is needed.

`role="separator"` with `aria-orientation` (the primitive Separator): the line runs across the group's
axis, so a horizontal group's separator is `vertical`, read from the group unless `orientation` is given.

buttons beside it; the group stretches it to their height. Not focusable and no role: it is text.

exports.name: CheckboxProps
exports.description:
Design-language slot `checkbox` (@kitora/theme core `CheckboxSlot`): the box's size, radius, empty
fill, checked sheen, shadow, tick size and focus ring read `var(--dk-checkbox-…, <Kitora value>)`,
so the default look is unchanged (see button.tsx).

Label wiring, two ways:
- pass `id` and point your own `<label htmlFor={id}>` at it: Base UI puts the
  id on the checkbox's hidden `<input>`, so a click on that label toggles the
  box and the label becomes its accessible name;
- or pass `label` and the checkbox renders the `<label>` beside itself
  (generating an id when you gave none). Without `label` the markup is
  exactly the bare control, as before.

`description` adds a line under the label, announced with the box (`aria-describedby`, after any
description the enclosing Field adds). The label / description contract is the same on `Switch` and
`RadioGroupItem` (see choice-label.ts).

Inside a `Field` the Field's label names it; inside a `CheckboxGroup` its
`value` joins the group's, and with `parent` it is the group's parent box
(mixed, drawn with a dash, while only some children are ticked).

exports.name: FieldOrientation
exports.description:
A form field: a label, a control (an `Input`, `Checkbox`, `Switch`, `RadioGroup` or `Slider` placed inside),
a description and an error, wired together. The label names the control and a press on it focuses or toggles
it, the description and the error are announced with it (`aria-describedby`), and the control reports
focus, change and validity back to the field, which writes `data-valid`, `data-invalid`, `data-touched`,
`data-dirty`, `data-filled`, `data-focused` and `data-disabled`. The styled controls already show `aria-invalid`.

Validation: `validate` returns a message (or an array of them) or `null`; `validationMode` picks `onSubmit`
(default, then on every change after a submit), `onBlur` or `onChange`; the browser's own constraints
(`required`, `type="email"`, `pattern`, `minLength`) validate first. Inside a `Form` the field blocks a failed submit.

exports.name: MaskInputProps
exports.description:
`MaskInput`: ui's `Input` formatting as the person types, on the primitives' `useMask` (`core/mask.ts`). It takes every
`Input` prop (size, read-only, the `input` design-language slot, Field wiring: inside a `Field` the label names it, the
description and error describe it and an invalid Field marks it), plus the mask's own:

- `mask`: a string in the token alphabet (`9` digit, `a` letter, `A` letter upper-cased, `*` letter or digit, `#` digit
  or sign; `\` escapes, `?` starts the optional tail), an array of literals and `RegExp` slots, or a function of the raw
  value (to switch masks by value). `tokens` adds custom tokens, `transform` rewrites every typed character.
- `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange(raw, display)`: the value is the raw string, only what was typed into the
  slots. `showMask` (`never` by default) shows the whole pattern always or on focus, with `placeholderChar`.
- `name` posts the raw value through a hidden input (`submit="raw"`, the default); `submit="display"` posts the
  formatted string from the visible input instead.

The placeholder shows the pattern (`(___) ___-____`) unless one is given. A value that is started but not complete is
invalid (a custom validity message, so a form or a Field refuses it) and, once the input has lost focus, `aria-invalid`;
a `required` empty value is the browser's own `valueMissing`. The mask must never be the only description of the
format: pair it with a label or a description that says what to type. A mask whose slots are all digits renders
`dir="ltr"` (the field mirrors in a right-to-left page, the digits do not) and asks for the numeric keyboard.

exports.description:
A meter: a scalar inside a known range (disk used, a strength, a battery), `role="meter"`. A bare number reads as a percentage;

exports.name: SliderMarks

`SliderControl` before the thumbs (so a thumb paints over a tick). Each mark has `data-value` and, when it lies in
the filled range (start to the value, or between a range's ends), `data-in-range`. Positions come from the

at that value. Horizontal marks are placed with `inset-inline-start`, so they mirror in right-to-left text the way
the thumbs do; vertical marks grow upward from the bottom. Pressing a mark or its label is a press on the track.

exports.name: Toggletip
exports.description:
A toggletip: an info button that opens a tooltip-looking bubble on click, Enter or Space (not on hover), so touch, keyboard and screen
reader users all reach the explanation a tooltip would hide from them. React Aria's `Toggletip` and Spectrum's `ContextualHelp` are the
reference. Built on the primitives' Popover (non-modal): Escape and a press outside close it, focus stays on the button (`initialFocus`

needs a heading, links or actions is a `Popover`.

exports.name: POPUP_MORPH_POSITIONER_CLASS
exports.description:
Classes for a popup that animates between the triggers of one popup (`morph` on `PopoverContent`, `TooltipContent`, `HoverCardContent`
and `DropdownMenuContent`, over the primitives' `Viewport`). The positioner moves and resizes with a transition (`adaptiveOrigin` needs a
CSS transition on the positioner to apply), and the popup's height follows the size the viewport writes (`--popup-height`) with a
transition. The popup keeps its own width and duration: a popup that should also animate its width takes `w-(--popup-width,auto)` in
its `className`. Reduced motion drops the transitions.

(`data-current`) slide and fade toward and from where the new trigger is (`data-activation-direction`, read into `--vx` / `--vy`).

On a coarse pointer (a finger) a row is at least 44px tall, the WCAG 2.5.5 / platform touch target; a mouse keeps today's ~28px row.

exports.description:
The read-only look of a field box that carries `data-readonly` (a combobox or autocomplete input group, a select trigger): the muted fill
of a read-only `Input` (`inputReadOnlyClassName` in input.tsx: the `input` slot's `--dk-input-readonly-bg`, `bg-muted/40` as the
fallback, the `dark:` copy so it replaces the dark field fill too) and a default cursor, so a value that cannot be changed does not look
changeable. Variant-scoped, so a box without `data-readonly` renders exactly as before.

exports.name: POSITIONER_PASSTHROUGH_KEYS
exports.description:
The primitives' Positioner options that every anchored ui content (`PopoverContent`, `HoverCardContent`, `TooltipContent`,
`DropdownMenuContent`, `ContextMenuContent`, and `MenubarContent` through the dropdown's) takes as its own props and hands to its
Positioner untouched: before, only `align` / `side` and their offsets were picked, so these fell into `...props` on the popup and a caller
had to recompose the parts to keep a popup inside a scroll box, pin it to a scrolling anchor, or place it `fixed`. One list, so the seven
files cannot drift; `anchor` stays a per-file pick because not every family takes one.

exports.description: One of the Positioner options in `POSITIONER_PASSTHROUGH_KEYS`.

exports.name: PositionerPassthrough
exports.description: The pass-through options as a family's Positioner types them: `PositionerPassthrough<PopoverPrimitive.Positioner.Props>`.

exports.name: POPUP_ARROW_CLASS
exports.description:
The arrow of an anchored popup with the popover look (a rotated square in the popup's fill and edge ring, behind the popup so only its
outer half shows): the dropdown menu's and the context menu's arrow, and now the popover's and the hover card's, one string so the four
stay alike. Physical insets appear only under `data-[side=left|right]` (a caller who placed the popup on a physical side); the logical
sides use `start` / `end`.
